en.title: Largest String After Swapping Adjacent Digits of the Same Parity
en.description:
You may only swap two adjacent digits with the same parity, any number of times. Return the largest digit string; all digits, including zeros, must be kept. For the original 0082663 the correct result is 8662003; the original example dropped the zeros.

The input/output protocol was compiled by this site, and missing numeric bounds are explicitly marked as site additions.
en.input: One line with a digit string of length 1..100000 containing only 0..9; leading zeros are allowed.
en.output: Output the largest digit string of the original length; leading zeros must not be removed.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: 9758601; 8662003; 2014. These answers have been checked by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Split the string into maximal runs of the same parity and output each run's digits from largest to smallest, counting them with 10 buckets.
